response.exception:
frappe.exceptions.PermissionError:
You are not permitted to access this resource. Login to accessFunction yob_storefront.api.catalog.get_categories is not whitelisted.
response.exc: <TRUNCATED - full python traceback as a JSON-encoded string>

notes: NOT the YOB envelope: there is no `message` wrapper and no `errors` array.
The wording 'is not whitelisted' is Frappe's generic text for 'whitelisted but not guest-allowed'. It does not mean the endpoint is missing.
The network layer must normalise this shape too. Branch on exc_type='PermissionError' + HTTP 403, never on the HTML-bearing detail text.
The response body contains a full server traceback. Never surface it to users and never log it verbatim.

notes: Also NOT the YOB envelope. Frappe rejects the request in init_request, before the endpoint runs.
400 + exc_type='CSRFTokenError' is the signal that the in-memory CSRF token is missing or stale; the correct recovery is to re-run get_session_context, not to log the user out.

checkout_payment.checkout_token_invalid: 404 - blank, unknown, or revoked checkout token.
checkout_payment.payment_request_stale: 409 - the cart changed since the obligation was issued; restart checkout.
checkout_payment.payment_reference_invalid: 422 - the payment could not be matched to a usable source/order.
checkout_payment.payment_method_unsupported: 422 - unknown method, or a known method that is not eligible now.
checkout_payment.payment_provider_not_configured: 500 - no Razorpay API key on the server.
checkout_payment.payment_provider_error: 500 - provider unreachable AFTER local commitment; details.retryable=true, details.sales_order present, order NOT rolled back.
checkout_payment.payment_already_processed: 409 - a different payment arrived for an already-settled obligation.
checkout_payment.payment_verification_failed: 500 - signature verification could not be completed.
checkout_payment.payment_not_captured: 422 - provider order/payment is not in a paid/captured state.
checkout_payment.payment_amount_mismatch: 409 - provider amount does not match the immutable obligation.
checkout_payment.payment_currency_mismatch: 409 - provider currency does not match the obligation.
checkout_payment.validation_failed: 422 - a required request field was missing.
checkout_payment.order_not_found: 404 - the referenced Sales Order no longer exists.
checkout_payment.customer_not_found: 404 - the customer behind the checkout link no longer exists.

notes: Complete registry, far larger than the four codes named in the OpenAPI examples. These strings are a stable part of the contract.

verification_levels.wire: Observed over HTTP through the edge proxy.
verification_levels.test: The real endpoint was executed in-process against seeded data, inside a rolled-back savepoint with frappe.db.commit suppressed and a deterministic Razorpay fake. Bodies are real envelopes from the real implementation, but no HTTP round trip and no live provider were involved.
verification_levels.source: Read from the implementation; not executed.

notes: Authenticated. Requires the `sid` session cookie AND `X-Frappe-CSRF-Token`.
Must traverse the edge proxy that sets `X-YOB-Original-Host`; a direct origin call answers 403 application_access_denied.
No request body. The server derives everything from the session: the browser never sends amount, currency, cart id or any fingerprint.
201 when a Payment Request was CREATED (first checkout, or a replacement because the cart changed). 200 when an existing open obligation was REUSED, with or without a rotated credential.
`payment_url` is a RELATIVE SPA path `/payment/<token>`; the public payment route must own that path.
The checkout credential expires 1 hour after issue.

A Payment Request's amount and currency are IMMUTABLE once issued. An unchanged cart reuses the same obligation and the same token; an expired credential rotates the token on the SAME obligation; a changed cart issues a REPLACEMENT obligation and revokes the old token immediately.

Precondition failures, 422 unless noted: cart_not_found (404), cart_empty, contact_required (field=contact_person), billing_address_required (field=billing_address), shipping_address_required (field=shipping_address, only when the cart is shippable).
PUBLIC (guest). Authorized solely by the unguessable checkout token.
Serves TWO source shapes. Branch on `data.source_doctype`.
Cart-backed (before payment initiation): source_doctype='Cart', with `cart`, `contact`, `billing_address`, `shipping_address` objects plus `cart_updated`, `removed_items`, `price_updated_items`.

Sales-Order-backed (after payment initiation committed the order): source_doctype='Sales Order', with a flat `items[]`, `order_status`, `docstatus`, and `billing_address`/`shipping_address` as NAME STRINGS rather than objects. This shape difference is deliberate and the SPA must handle both.
After the Payment Request becomes Sales-Order-backed the Cart is no longer payment truth. It is not read, compared or revalidated, and a later cart change cannot invalidate the committed payment.
`amount`/`currency` always come from the immutable Payment Request, in normal business units (e.g. 135.0 INR) -- NOT provider units.
The token is NOT revoked when the source moves Cart -> Sales Order, so a browser refresh of /payment/:token keeps working and Pay Later orders remain payable later.
`payment_methods[]` is server-eligible only; render exactly this list.

This checkout link is not valid.
Your cart has changed since this payment was started. Please return to the cart and continue again.

notes: PUBLIC (guest). Authorized solely by the checkout token.
The browser sends ONLY `token` and `payment_method`. It never sends amount, currency, cart, sales order or razorpay order id -- all are derived server-side from the immutable Payment Request.
`payment_method` is the Payment Method's `name` (e.g. 'Pay Later', 'Razorpay'), i.e. the `name` field from `payment_methods[]` -- not `method_code`.
Eligibility is re-checked authoritatively on every call. A method that was offered earlier but is no longer eligible is refused, and no order is created.
Commits the cart to exactly ONE Draft Sales Order, idempotently. Repeated calls -- Pay Later then Razorpay, or a retry after failure -- converge on the same Sales Order and the same provider order.

Razorpay `amount` is in PROVIDER UNITS (paise: 13500 == INR 135.00). Pay Later `amount` is the normal business amount (135.0). This difference is intentional: the Razorpay value is passed straight to the checkout widget.

A provider failure AFTER the local commitment returns payment_provider_error with `details.retryable = true` and `details.sales_order`. The Sales Order was NOT rolled back -- do not show the user 'order failed'; offer a retry.

errors.detail: This payment method is not supported.
This payment method is not available for this order.
Your cart has changed since this payment was started. Please return to the cart and continue again.
We could not reach the payment provider. Your order is saved -- please try paying again.

notes: PUBLIC (guest). Authorized by Razorpay's HMAC signature, verified server-side. NO checkout token is accepted or required: the obligation is resolved through the provider order id.
All three fields are required; a missing one answers validation_failed with `field` naming the first missing one.

Idempotent. Re-verifying the SAME payment id returns the same success body with notice 'Payment already processed.'. A DIFFERENT payment against an already-settled obligation is refused with payment_already_processed (409).
Settlement never creates a Sales Order -- it settles the one that process_payment already committed.
The frontend's claim of success is never trusted; the server independently fetches and validates the provider order and payment.

notes: Authenticated. Eligibility is centralized server-side; the `customer` query parameter is accepted for backward compatibility only and is overwritten with the authenticated Customer (a mismatching value is rejected outright).
